setup.title: First run
setup.intro: A few things are enough: the setup code, where your antenna is, your time zone and an admin password.
setup.position_help: Antenna position, for example copied from a right-click on OpenStreetMap. It is used for distances and range, and is never sent anywhere.
setup.code_help: Shown at the end of install.sh and in the logs (docker compose logs app). To show it again: docker compose exec app php bin/setup-code.php. It makes sure only the person running the server becomes admin.
setup.err.code: Wrong setup code: see the end of install.sh, or run docker compose exec app php bin/setup-code.php.
setup.err.name: Give the station a name (48 characters max).
setup.err.password_match: The two passwords do not match.
setup.done.title: Setup complete
setup.done.intro: One step left: tell AIS-catcher to send its data to AISSeaStats.
setup.done.token_once: Write this token down now: it will not be shown again. You can generate a new one from the admin page.
setup.done.cli: AIS-catcher on the command line or as a service: add these options to your current command (the "..."), do not run it as is
setup.done.meta: On the command line, keep -M DTM (signal level, timestamps, flag country). In managed mode this is usually sent already; otherwise the flag is derived from the MMSI. The first statistics appear within a minute.
admin.login_locked: Too many failed attempts: try again in {n} min (or reset the password with bin/reset-admin.php).
admin.lost_password: Lost password: in the install folder, docker compose exec app php bin/reset-admin.php (from anywhere: docker exec -it aisseastats-app-1 php bin/reset-admin.php)
admin.invalid_tiles: The tile URL must start with https:// and contain {z}, {x} and {y}.
admin.invalid_zone: Invalid zone: name, position and radius (0 to 200 NM) are required; N, NE, E… are reserved names.
admin.token_new: New token generated. Update the AIS-catcher configuration.
admin.password_short: This password is short (fewer than 8 characters): fine on a home network, but choose a longer one if the page can be reached from the Internet. Admin → Password changes it.
admin.mmsi_deleted: All data for MMSI {m} has been deleted.
admin.reset_done: All collected data has been deleted.
admin.error: Something went wrong, check the container logs.
admin.worker_down: Background jobs have stopped: check the "worker" container (docker compose ps).
admin.ingest_help: Line to add to AIS-catcher. The token is not stored in clear text; generate a new one if you lost it.
admin.token_confirm: The old token will stop working immediately. Continue?
admin.max_range_help: Positions further away are ignored (bogus messages). Tropospheric ducting can exceed 1,000 NM. Beyond 50 NM, a position only counts for range if the vessel was received shortly before at a consistent position.
admin.gap_help: Silence after which a vessel is considered gone.
admin.retention_help: Tracks are deleted after that; statistics are kept.
admin.enrich: Look up vessel photos online (Wikimedia Commons and Wikidata)
admin.position_round_help: The statistics page and its API show the station rounded to 0.01°, handy when the antenna is at home and the page is public. Distances and range still use the exact position.
admin.rules_help: Indicative rules: AIS does not reliably say whether a vessel is military or a luxury yacht.
admin.rule_military: AIS type 35 or MMSI prefix from the list
admin.rule_yacht: sailing or pleasure craft longer than below
admin.rule_hazmat: cargo and tankers, categories A to D
admin.military_prefixes_help: One prefix per line, 3 to 9 digits.
admin.watchlist_help: One MMSI or exact name per line.
admin.zones_help: By default a route goes from one sector (N, NE…) to another. Add named zones (lock, port, town) for more meaningful routes: click the map to place the centre.
admin.delete_mmsi_confirm: Permanently delete all data for this vessel?
admin.delete_mmsi_help: Removes this vessel and its whole history from the statistics.
admin.reset_confirm: Delete all collected statistics? Settings are kept.
admin.reset_help: Type RESET. Useful after a trial run with the simulator.
setup.import_help: If AIS-catcher runs in managed mode, its config.json file already holds the station name and position. Pick the file or paste its content: it is read in your browser and never sent anywhere.
setup.import_cmd: cat <AIS-catcher config folder>/config.json   (mounted as /config in the Docker container)
http.managed_intro: In AIS-catcher: Output → HTTP tab → add an output, then fill in the fields like this:
http.id: optional: station name, shown in the ingestion log
http.response: either way (shows AISSeaStats' reply in the AIS-catcher log, handy to check)
http.save: Keep "Active" on, then save with the floppy-disk icon at the top right: while the "You have unsaved changes" banner shows, nothing is applied.
http.mdns_warning: You are using a .local address. If AIS-catcher runs in Docker, it cannot resolve .local names: in the URL, use the Pi's IP address, or its local DNS name without .local (e.g. from Pi-hole), followed by :8095.
http.show_help: Show the fields to fill in AIS-catcher
fleet.hint: Click a row to see the vessels behind it.
list.subtitle: {n} vessels · {p}
list.truncated: List limited to the first 300 vessels.
admin.photos_help: Free photos are looked up automatically on Wikimedia Commons and Wikidata, but many fishing boats and pleasure craft are not there. Add your own photos here (JPEG, PNG or WebP, 3 MB max): they are stored in the database and take priority. Only use photos you have the rights to.
admin.photo_err_upload: No file received, or the upload failed.
admin.photo_err_type: Unknown format: use a JPEG, PNG or WebP image.
admin.dest_help: Destinations are typed freely by the crew: the same port comes in several forms (FRSML, SAINT-MALO, ST.MALO…). Spaces and punctuation are already ignored, and meaningless values (0, Q, NONE…) are grouped as "Unknown". Here, group the other variants under one name, ideally the port's UN/LOCODE (FRSML, FRCER…). Grouping also applies to data already received.
admin.db_size_help: “Data” is the size of the statistics. MariaDB's Docker volume is bigger (about 100 to 130 MB on a new install): it also holds fixed-size files, including the transaction log ({log}). This is normal; only the data grows with the history.
alert.down_text: No AIS message received for {d} (last one at {t}). Check AIS-catcher, the receiver and the antenna.
alert.up_text: AIS messages are coming in again, after an outage of {d}.
alert.test_text: AISSeaStats alerts work. Last AIS message received: {t}.
admin.alerts_help: Get a message when the station has received nothing for a while, and another one when reception comes back. One alert per outage. Fill in one or more channels, save, then “Send a test”.
admin.alert_none: No channel configured: fill in at least ntfy, Telegram, the webhook or e-mail.
admin.alert_state_down: Outage in progress, alert sent {a} ago.
admin.alert_ntfy_help: Install the ntfy app (Android, iPhone) and subscribe to the topic chosen here. On the public ntfy.sh server anyone who knows the topic name can read it: pick a name that is hard to guess. The token is only needed for a protected server.
admin.alert_telegram_help: Create a bot with @BotFather (/newbot command), which gives you the token. Send a message to your bot, then open https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/getUpdates: the chat ID is the “chat” → “id” value.
admin.alert_webhook_help: A JSON POST is sent to this address. It holds the fields expected by Discord (content), Slack and Mattermost (text), Gotify (title, message, priority) and Home Assistant (event, station, last_message…). For Gotify, add ?token=… to the URL.
admin.alert_email_help: Your mail provider’s outgoing (SMTP) server. Gmail: smtp.gmail.com, port 587, STARTTLS, with an “app password”. Several recipients allowed, separated by commas.
admin.alert_heartbeat_help: The alerts above cannot be sent if the Pi is off or offline. To cover that case, enter the “push” URL of an external monitoring service (healthchecks.io, Uptime Kuma in Push mode…): it is called every 5 minutes while reception works, and that service warns you when the calls stop.
vessel.no_name: Name not received yet: it only comes in the vessel's identity message (AIS type 5, every 6 minutes), which is longer and so more often lost at the edge of range. It will show as soon as it is received.
vessel.no_name_b: Name not received yet: for a class B vessel it only comes in the identity message (AIS type 24, every 6 minutes). It will show as soon as it is received.
admin.debug_help: To understand missing data (name, type…), records the raw messages received from AIS-catcher for a few vessels and shows them. The capture stops by itself; messages are deleted after 7 days.
admin.debug_mmsi_help: Up to 20, separated by commas. Empty: every vessel, for 1 h at most.
admin.debug_no_static: No identity message (type 5, 19 or 24): the antenna has not received the name.
admin.debug_types_help: AIS types: 1, 2, 3 position (class A) · 5 identity and voyage (name, type, destination) · 18, 19 position (class B) · 24 identity (class B) · 8 200/10 inland data (ENI, dimensions) · 4 base station · 21 aid to navigation.
admin.debug_bad_mmsi: Invalid MMSI: 9 digits, separated by commas.
admin.debuglog_help: Dated JSON Lines files, written live during the capture and kept 30 days in {d} (Docker volume "debug-logs", kept across updates). Readable with grep or jq.
prop.title: Exceptional propagation:
range.tropo_hint: Beyond the horizon, reception depends on tropospheric propagation, which changes with the weather. Forecast:
reg.title: Regulars
reg.hint: Vessels that come back most regularly (at least 4 passages)
reg.empty: Not enough passages yet: a vessel needs at least 4 in the period.
heat.title: Busiest hours
heat.note: Unique vessels per hour, averaged over {days} days (station local time; hours without any message are not counted). Peak: {best} ({bv}) · quietest: {low} ({lv}).
up.title: Station reception
up.hint: An hour without any message can be an outage (receiver, antenna, AIS-catcher, network) or simply no traffic in a quiet area. To be warned of an outage: Admin → Alerts.
admin.public_url_help: For example https://ais.example.org. Used for the links in alerts and summaries (vessel card) and for Home Assistant's "Visit" link. Leave empty if the page cannot be reached from the Internet.
admin.public_url_invalid: Invalid public address: it must start with http:// or https://.
admin.military_no_block: No MMSI block is reserved for military vessels: each country assigns its own (often in its normal MID range), and many warships do not transmit, or transmit with type 35. Add the prefixes known for your area here.
admin.mqtt_help: Publishes the station state (vessels today, active, messages, range, reception…) to an MQTT server, with Home Assistant discovery: an "AISSeaStats" device and its sensors appear by themselves. Alerts and summaries can be sent there too (see the channels below). No message per vessel.
admin.mqtt_test_ok: connected, a test message was published to {t}.
admin.mqtt_state_wait: Waiting for the next worker run (less than a minute).
admin.mqtt_tls_verify: Check the server certificate (untick for a self-signed certificate on your home network)
admin.mqtt_topics: "state" (JSON, retained, every minute), "event" (alerts and summaries, QoS 1), "availability" (online / offline; offline is sent by the server if the worker stops).
admin.mqtt_f_mqtt_prefix: topic prefix (letters, digits, - and _, separated by /)
admin.mqtt_f_mqtt_discovery_prefix: discovery prefix (letters, digits, - and _, separated by /)
admin.notify_help: Uses the channels set in "Alerts" (ntfy, Telegram, webhook, e-mail) and MQTT. Each vessel alerts once per passage and reason; several reasons make one message.
admin.notify_no_channel: No channel set for summaries: set up a channel in "Alerts" or MQTT, and tick it in the channel table.
admin.notify_triggers_help: Reasons come from the "Interesting vessels" rules below (a reason whose rule is off never fires). First visit: a vessel never seen before (after one week of history). Distress: sent even during quiet hours.
admin.notify_quiet_help: During quiet hours, or beyond the maximum per hour, alerts are only noted in the log below (they are not sent later).
admin.notify_routes_help: Choose where each kind of message goes. Reception = "no data" and "reception restored" alerts.
admin.notify_routes_greyed: Greyed channels are not set up yet: they receive nothing.
admin.notify_log_empty: No vessel alert or summary yet.
admin.notify_bad_time: Invalid time: use the HH:MM format.
notify.prop_text: Today's range {d} against {u} usually; {n} vessels received well beyond the usual range.
const.title: Constellation
const.hint_dest: The station in the centre; around it, the destinations declared by the vessels seen in the period (size = number of vessels) and, as small bubbles, their types. Click a bubble to see the vessels; + and − to zoom.
const.hint_ports: Ports linked by the vessels: when a vessel changes its destination, the old port is linked to the new one (arrow in the direction of travel, width = vessels). Click an arrow or a port to see the vessels.
const.none_dest: No destination declared in this period.
const.none_ports: No links yet: the history of destinations is collected since version 1.2.0. Come back in a few days.
rec.title: Records
sig.title: Signal and distance
sig.none: No data yet for this period: the signal level is recorded since version 1.2.0, when AIS-catcher sends it (signalpower field).
sig.note: {n} positions with a signal level, up to {d}.
sig.hint: Mean level received by distance of the vessel, in 2 NM bins. Useful to tune the antenna or the gain and compare before / after a change (pick the period), or to spot a masked direction.
const.zoom_in: Zoom in (or double click, Ctrl + wheel, pinch)
admin.ports_help: Many vessels declare their destination as a UN/LOCODE code (NLRTM, FRSML, IEORK…). This button downloads, from your station, UNECE's official list (about 7 MB, an extract published on GitHub by datasets/un-locode) and keeps the names of its 17,000 or so ports: NLRTM becomes "Rotterdam" everywhere. The list is not shipped with AISSeaStats (its licence does not clearly allow redistributing it); names in your dictionary keep priority. Source:
admin.ports_none: List not downloaded: codes are shown as they are.
admin.ports_import: Fill in the names of UN/LOCODE ports
admin.ports_failed: Download failed: {e}. The current list is kept.
remarkable.empty_tag: No recent passage for this kind of vessel.
